title: Setup
text: Please complete the following steps before the workshop so we can dive straight into the material.

title: Setup
text:
Accounts

GitHub account — needed to clone and work with the workshop materials. Sign up at https://github.com if you don’t have one.
Posit AI account — we’ll use Posit Assistant in Positron during the workshop. If you don’t already have one, create a free account at https://posit.ai. Use the same email address you registered for the workshop with, because this is how we attach your workshop credits.

title: Setup
text:
Software requirements

Positron
We’ll be live-coding in Positron. Download and install the latest Positron (2026.07 or newer) from https://positron.posit.co/download.
The following extensions are the ones we’ll be relying on and Positron already ships with them — nothing extra to install.

Quarto
Air
Posit Assistant

Quarto (latest release)
We’ll rely on recent features of Quarto, so please make sure you have the latest version installed — v1.10 or later. Check your version with:
quarto --version
Download at: https://quarto.org/docs/download/
R or Python
Bring whichever language you usually use with Quarto. For R, we recommend R 4.6 or later with an up-to-date tidyverse:
install.packages("tidyverse")
Git
We’ll clone workshop materials and discuss version control workflows. If you don’t already have Git, install it from https://git-scm.com/downloads.
Posit AI
In Positron, open the Command Palette and run Authentication: Configure Language Model Providers, choose Posit AI, and sign in through your browser. That’s it! During the workshop, usage draws from the workshop’s credit pool first, not your personal balance.

title: Setup
text:
Check your setup
Before the workshop, open a terminal in Positron and confirm the following run without errors:
quarto --version   # 1.10 or later
git --version
Then create and render a test document:
quarto create document test-setup
cd test-setup
quarto render test-setup.qmd --to html
quarto render test-setup.qmd --to typst
If both renders succeed, you’re all set. Typst is bundled with Quarto, so no separate installation is needed.

title: Setup
text:
Having trouble?
If you run into installation issues, please post on the workshop thread on Posit Community before the workshop and we’ll help you get sorted.

title: Level up your Quarto: Patterns, templates, and tooling
text:
Instructors
Charlotte Wickham is a Senior Developer Advocate at Posit with a focus on Quarto. Before Posit, she taught Statistics and Data Science at Oregon State University. 
Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel is Professor of the Practice at Duke University in the Department of Statistical Science and Senior Developer Advocate at Posit, PBC, where she’s part of the tidyverse team. Mine is a co-author of influential open textbooks like R for Data Science and OpenIntro Statistics, and her contributions to education and open science have earned her several accolades, including the Waller Education Award by the American Statistical Association, the Robert V. Hogg Award by the Mathematical Association of America, and the Pickard Award by Harvard University’s Department of Statistics.

title: Level up your Quarto: Patterns, templates, and tooling
text:
Description
This workshop is designed for Quarto users who want to update and extend their Quarto mastery. Led by Charlotte Wickham and Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel, this workshop will introduce new features of Quarto as well as blend practical recipes with conceptual understanding, so you can both copy–paste what works and understand why it works. Rather than a linear tour of Quarto features, the workshop is organized as a collection of focused, reusable patterns—each one solving a real authoring or publishing problem you’re likely to encounter.
Themes will include:

Design once, use anywhere: Learn how to work effectively with light and dark modes, brands, and renderings, and how to share a consistent brand across multiple Quarto projects without duplication or fragility.
Build reusable structures: Use template partials to factor out repeated content and layouts, making large or long-lived projects easier to maintain and evolve.
Understand why Typst matters: Explore why Typst deserves a place on your radar, with concrete “quick wins” that show how it can dramatically simplify PDF generation.
Work productively in Positron: Pick up Positron- and Quarto-specific productivity tips, including auto-formatting with Air, and practical ways to incorporate LLMs into your Quarto workflow.
Master freezing and reproducibility: Demystify freeze—when to check it in to version control, when to refresh it, and how to use it intentionally to balance reproducibility, performance, and collaboration.

By the end of the workshop, you’ll have a curated set of Quarto recipes and a mental model for how the pieces fit together. You’ll leave the workshop equipped to create more polished documents, scale your workflows across projects and teams, and make deliberate, informed choices about tools, formats, and authoring strategies.
